claims.text: A computer's processor executes only machine code, so a program written in an assembly or a high-level language must be translated into machine code before it can run.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: An assembler translates an assembly language program into machine code one mnemonic at a time; a compiler translates a whole high-level program into machine code before any of it runs; an interpreter translates and executes a high-level program one statement at a time at run time.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Compiling suits a finished program distributed to many users: the compiled file runs on its own at the machine's own speed, and the source code is not given away.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Interpreting suits development: each edit is tested immediately with no compile step, and the interpreter stops at a statement's error so the programmer can fix it at once.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: The drawbacks sit opposite the benefits: a compiled program must be recompiled for each change and for each different type of machine, and an interpreted program runs slower and needs the interpreter present wherever it runs.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A high-level language program may be translated partly by compiling and partly by interpreting: the source is compiled into an intermediate code, and a matching interpreter executes that code at run time.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: A context-sensitive prompt suggests what can be written next at the current point in the code, and auto-completion finishes the word being typed from the available names.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Dynamic syntax checking flags syntax errors as the code is typed, so errors are caught before a run.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: IDE debugging tools include breakpoints, where execution pauses; single stepping, which executes one statement at a time; and variable watch windows, which display chosen variables' values as the program runs.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).

claims.text: Prettyprint presents code with consistent layout, and expand and collapse code blocks hide and show sections, so a long program stays readable.

verification.method: Authored originally for 9618 AS under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires semantic review (RS-28).
